extraction.citation: dos Santos GAC, Bastos VK, Razzolini MTP (2026). WASH policy responses for homeless populations during the COVID-19 pandemic: a global review with emphasis on Brazil. Journal of Water, Sanitation and Hygiene for Development 16(9):862-876.
extraction.country: Brazil (emphasis); global (72 of 94 documents international, USA 26)
extraction.legal_system: mixed (Brazil civil law; USA and other common law jurisdictions)
extraction.service_provider: municipal and state governments and public-health services (emergency mobile toilets, showers, handwashing stations, hotel isolation, hygiene kits); NGOs
extraction.regulatory_model: Brazil: National Policy for the Homeless Population (Decree 7.053/2009) recognises rights but has no WASH-specific or emergency operational provisions; responses ran through state and municipal decrees (Sao Paulo Decree 59.283/2020, Rio de Janeiro State Law 8.823/2020, Salvador Decree 32.345/2020) and varied with local capacity; funding went to cash aid (Auxilio Emergencial) rather than WASH infrastructure. USA: decentralised municipal measures. Urban rules that criminalise public-space use are cited (Neves-Silva & Heller 2016)
extraction.population: people experiencing homelessness (street and sheltered) during the COVID-19 pandemic, 2020-2024
extraction.sample_size: 94 documents analysed (36 peer-reviewed articles, 30 institutional reports, 20 governmental legal and regulatory documents, 9 technical reports and grey literature); flow (Figure 1): 150 records, 5 duplicates removed, 145 screened, 95 assessed in full text, 0 excluded at full text, 1 excluded in the analysis (agricultural water), 94 analysed
extraction.effect_measure: narrative synthesis of documents coded on four axes (Table 1: Social Context 39, Sustainability and Political Integration 23, Immediate Access 19, Equity and Inclusion 12, combined 1); no effect estimate
extraction.effect_estimate: An 'inequality of attention': responses were emergency and temporary (mobile toilets and showers, hotel isolation, handwashing stations, hygiene kits), not integrated with housing or social protection. Brazil's national policy (Decree 7.053/2009) recognises rights but has no WASH-specific or emergency operational provisions; state and municipal decrees (Sao Paulo, Rio de Janeiro State, Salvador) filled the gap unevenly according to local capacity; funding went to cash aid rather than WASH infrastructure; policy was fragmented and curative rather than preventive. The USA relied on decentralised municipal measures. The authors recommend funded, permanent WASH inside housing models such as Housing First, and intersectoral governance. No measured access outcome.
extraction.extraction_sample_size: 94 documents analysed (95 assessed in full text; the document-type and geographic counts each sum to 95)
extraction.model_type: documentary and integrative review (document analysis coded on four axes)
extraction.study_design: documentary and integrative review with a stated four-database search (Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, Google Scholar plus institutional and governmental repositories, Jan-Mar 2024; English, Portuguese, Spanish), criteria and a PRISMA-style flow diagram; no protocol or registration, duplicate screening or extraction, or appraisal of the sources described; secondary evidence
extraction.risk_of_bias_rating: Critically Low (appraised 2026-10-13 against the official AMSTAR 2 checklist on the full text; item-level answers in 04_quality/appraisal_forms/S1168_AMSTAR2.md; critical items 2 (no protocol), 7 (no list of excluded studies), 9 (no appraisal of the sources) and 13 are flawed and item 4 is only partly met). Eligibility is a hybrid judgment: a documentary review with a stated multi-database search and flow diagram, kept under AMSTAR 2 like S418; the PI ruled it eligible on 2026-10-14 (A23).

extraction.extraction_note: Added by the PI's A23 ruling of 2026-10-14 (include: it examines legal recognition and statutory and decree gaps and reports a database search and flow diagram), after the AI read all 15 pages of the published article that the researcher dropped in the Drive inbox on 2026-10-13 (text and tables as page images; PDF not committed; assessment note 02_screening/full_text/UNASSESSED_RECORD_R4A7F8709BEDE_READ_2026-10-13.md). The record had passed title/abstract screening but was never assessed at full text (not_retrievable; one of the 1,383 never-assessed records at the 2026-09-28 closure), so this is a recorded exception to that closure. Limitations noted at the time: the counts do not reconcile (the flow diagram ends at 94 but the document-type counts 36+30+20+9 and the geographic counts 72+23 each sum to 95, and the type percentages sum to 101.1%); the stated search window is Jan-Mar 2024 but the reference list has access dates from Nov 2025 to 18 Aug 2026; Table S1 (the list of documents) was not supplied, so the corpus could not be checked; none of 14 cited peer-reviewed works matched the project's own pool of records. No effect_sizes.csv row (no measured outcome). record_id R4A7F8709BEDE.

evidence_map.evidence_level: Documentary and integrative review with a stated four-database search and flow diagram (94 documents: 36 peer-reviewed articles, 30 institutional reports, 20 governmental legal and regulatory documents, 9 technical reports) of WASH policy responses for people experiencing homelessness during COVID-19, with emphasis on Brazil; no protocol, duplicate screening or appraisal of the sources; AMSTAR 2 Critically Low; read in full text 2026-10-13.

evidence_map.institutional_context: National Policy for the Homeless Population (Brazil, Decree 7.053/2009) without WASH-specific operational provisions; state and municipal emergency decrees; funding through cash aid rather than WASH infrastructure; decentralised municipal measures in the USA; fragmented, emergency and curative policy
